title: Scalar retractions induce equivariant continuous cochain projections
statement:
Let $E\subseteq F\subseteq L$ be fields [def-weil-field], all with topologies making their field operations continuous, and assume the inclusions are continuous. Let $p:L\to F$ be a continuous $E$-linear map with $p(a)=a$ for all $a\in F$. Let $d\geq0$, and let $G$ be a topological group (multiplication and inversion continuous) acting on $E^d$ by $E$-linear automorphisms with a jointly continuous action. On $V_L=L^d$ and $V_F=F^d$, with their product topologies, use the actions given by the same matrices with entries in $E$. Write $i:V_F\hookrightarrow V_L$ for coordinate inclusion, and define
$$P:V_L\to V_F,\quad P((x_j)_{j<d})=(p(x_j))_{j<d},\qquad Q=1-iP:V_L\to V_L.$$
Then the two scalar-extended actions are jointly continuous, $i,P,Q$ are continuous $E$-linear $G$-equivariant maps, $Pi=1$, and $Qi=0$. For every $k\geq0$, postcomposition defines $E$-linear maps $P_*,i_*,Q_*$ on both the homogeneous and the inhomogeneous continuous cochains $B^k(G,V)$ and $C^k(G,V)$ of [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates]. They satisfy
$$P_*\delta=\delta P_*,\quad P_*d=dP_*,\quad P_*i_*=1,\quad Q_*=1-i_*P_*,$$
with the analogous differential identities for $i_*$ and $Q_*$. These maps commute with restriction to every subgroup with its induced topology and with both coordinate maps $\Phi,\Psi$ of that node. In particular, if $f:G^{k+1}\to V_L$ is a continuous diagonally equivariant homogeneous cocycle, then $P_*f$ is such a cocycle with values in $V_F$, and $Q_*f$ is one with values in $V_L$; on every subset where $f$ has values in $i(V_F)$, $Q_*f$ vanishes. These assertions include $d=0$ and cochain degree zero and require no multiplicativity of $p$ and no completeness of any field.

proof.text: Write $e_b$ for the standard basis vectors and $a_{ab}(g)=(g e_b)_a\in E$. Each $a_{ab}:G\to E$ is continuous: compose $g\mapsto(g,e_b)$, the given jointly continuous action on $E^d$, and coordinate evaluation. For $K=F,L$, the extended action is $(gx)_a=\sum_{b<d}a_{ab}(g)x_b$, with coefficients included in $K$. These coordinate functions on $G\times K^d$ are continuous finite sums of products, by the continuous inclusion $E\to K$ and the continuous field operations. The product topology therefore makes the action jointly continuous. The matrix identities $A(gh)=A(g)A(h)$ and $A(1)=I$, already valid over $E$, remain identities over $K$; hence these really are actions by $K$-linear automorphisms, and in particular by $E$-linear automorphisms. Addition and $E$-scalar multiplication on $K^d$ are continuous by the same coordinate test.

proof.text: Each coordinate of $i$ is the continuous inclusion $F\to L$, and each coordinate of $P$ is $p$ after coordinate evaluation, so both maps are continuous and $E$-linear. Subtraction in $L^d$ then makes $Q=1-iP$ continuous and $E$-linear. For all $g,x,a$, $P(gx)_a=p(\sum_b a_{ab}(g)x_b)=\sum_b a_{ab}(g)p(x_b)=(gP(x))_a$, using only $E$-linearity of $p$. The same matrix formula gives $i(gy)=g i(y)$. Subtracting the equivariance identities for $1$ and $iP$ gives equivariance of $Q$. Since $p$ fixes $F$, $Pi(y)=y$ coordinatewise, and $Qi(y)=i(y)-iPi(y)=0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-joint-continuous-coordinate-naturality] with $H=J=G$, $h=\operatorname{id}$, and successively $(V,W,u)=(V_L,V_F,P),(V_F,V_L,i),(V_L,V_L,Q)$. The topological vector space and jointly continuous action hypotheses hold by step 1; the continuous $E$-linear intertwining hypothesis holds by step 2. Its formulas are precisely postcomposition, so they define the required linear maps on both cochain spaces, preserving continuity and homogeneous equivariance. Its two differential identities give $P_*\delta=\delta P_*$ and $P_*d=dP_*$ and the analogous identities for $i_*,Q_*$. Its last two identities give commutation with both $\Phi$ and $\Psi$. The cited statement includes degree zero, where the inhomogeneous map is $u$ itself and $d v(g)=gv-v$.

proof.text: For either kind of cochain $c$, evaluation at each tuple $t$ gives $(P_*i_*c)(t)=P(i(c(t)))=c(t)$. Likewise $(Q_*c)(t)=Q(c(t))=c(t)-i(P(c(t)))=((1-i_*P_*)c)(t)$. Equality of functions gives $P_*i_*=1$ and $Q_*=1-i_*P_*$ in every degree. In degree zero these are the same identities on vectors (or on equivariant functions $G\to V$ in the homogeneous convention).

proof.text: Let $H\subseteq G$ have the induced topology. Its inclusion $h:H\to G$ is continuous, and its multiplication and inversion are restrictions of the continuous operations of $G$. The restricted action is jointly continuous by composing $H\times V\to G\times V$ with the action; all three coefficient maps remain equivariant. Restriction means precomposition with $h$ in every argument: for any of $u=P,i,Q$, $u(c(h(t_0),\ldots,h(t_k)))=(u\circ c)(h(t_0),\ldots,h(t_k))$, with $k$ arguments in the inhomogeneous case. This proves the asserted commutation with restriction. If $\delta f=0$, step 3 gives $\delta(P_*f)=P_*(0)=0$ and $\delta(Q_*f)=Q_*(0)=0$; their continuity and equivariance were also established there. At any tuple where $f(t)=i(y)$, $Q_*f(t)=Qi(y)=0$ by step 2.

proof.text: When $d=0$, each coefficient vector space is the zero vector space; all coordinate assertions are vacuous and all cochain spaces are zero, so every displayed identity still holds. For degree zero, the formulas in steps 3–5 explicitly cover both conventions. The argument uses $p$ only through continuity, additivity, $E$-homogeneity and its identity on $F$; it uses no multiplicativity or completeness.
